title: Ops sprint lane capture — regional capacity cadence and hedging sketches
body:
Meeting: Weekly Ops Sprint Lane (sketch + working notes)
Date: 2026-08-18
Facilitator: Aria Chen
Attendees: Aria Chen, Diego Martinez, Priya Kapoor, Liam O'Neill, Maya Singh, (notes from SRE shift)

Purpose: capture lightweight, tactical decisions and open questions for regional GPU capacity cadence, hedging experiments, and prewarm runbook fragments. This is a working scratchpad — not final. Use this to push quick wins into JIRA.

High-level summary
- Observed steady traffic growth in APAC region this week (~9% week-over-week token throughput). EU and US steady.
- Prewarming experiments in us-west show ~18% reduction in tail latency for 90th/95th when warm pools are >30% primed for common seq len 512 workloads.
- We should run a short hedging window next week for APAC (48 hours) using opportunistic reserved warm slots + controlled backfill.
- Immediate follow-ups: (1) finalize hedging rollout doc; (2) small change to autobalancer to prefer warm-pinned hosts for interactive tiers; (3) validate cost delta for hedging with finance.

Telemetry snapshot (this meeting)
- Global 1hr QPS median: 1.8k requests/s (text-gen); token rate +7% last 7d.
- us-west steady margin: 14% spare GPU capacity (after reserving Dedicated commitments).
- eu-central margin: 9% spare. apac-sg margin: 5% spare (high growth, highest variance).
- Tail latency 95th global (interactive): 280ms; us-west 95th: 240ms; apac-sg 95th: 360ms.
- Prewarm hit-rate (us-west experiment): 0.32 overall, but 0.58 for seq len 512 templates.

Quick analysis + implications
- APAC margin at 5% is fragile. If growth continues like the last two weeks, we'll hit <2% spare in ~10 days which increases preemptions and degrades tail latencies.
- Prewarming works well for predictable templates; benefit is workload dependent. We should extend telemetry to tag request templates so we can predict prewarm ROI by customer route.
- Hedging (short-term capacity reservation across regions) looks promising: shift low-priority burst traffic to us-west as buffer when APAC spikes, with automatic rollback if cross-region capacity costs exceed threshold.

Scenarios run during meeting (sketch simulation)
1) Mild spike (20% uplift APAC) — with current margins: apac hits negative spare in 18 hours; enabling opportunistic backfill from us-west reduces negative window to 6 hours. Cost increase: ~6% during window.
2) Severe spike (60% uplift APAC) — cross-region hedging delays failure by 36 hours but costs escalate ~28%; requires emergency procurement if sustained.
3) Flash burst (3x QPS for 3 minutes) — prewarm baseline reduces tail by ~40% for templated requests; non-templated requests still suffer.

Decisions taken (quick)
- Roll hedging trial in APAC for next week (48-hour window) using: 20% reserved warm slots in us-west, autobalancer preference, and cost guard rails. Owner: Diego Martinez.
- Add template-level telemetry flag to request tracing so prewarm ROI can be attributed. Owner: Priya Kapoor. Ticket: JIRA-OPS-4123.
- Small autobalancer tweak (prefer warm-pinned hosts for interactive-tier routes, preserve Dedicated isolation) — quick patch scheduled. Owner: Liam O'Neill. PR: linked.

Open risks / questions
- Cost sensitivity: Finance needs a precise estimate for hedging costs vs customer SLA impact if we do nothing. Maya to run week-end cost sim and share. Ticket: JIRA-OPS-4188.
- Data locality / compliance: Cross-region rerouting for some enterprise routes needs legal sign-off; we must ensure opt-out routes are enforced.
- Prewarm capacity accounting: where to book the cost? Shared pool or per-customer? Need product input.

Runbook fragment (working)
- Trigger: apac-sg spare capacity <6% sustained for 2h AND p95 > 300ms for interactive routes.
- Action: enable hedge mode for the region (manual toggle for first trial):
  - Allocate 20% warm reserve in us-west (ephemeral allocation job).
  - Set autobalancer bias +0.25 toward warm-pinned hosts for interactive-tier routes.
  - Enable conservative backfill for batch-only low-priority traffic.
- Monitoring: dashboard panel "Hedge window" with spare capacity, cross-region cost burn rate, and rollback flag. Pager if cross-region cost > budgeted threshold for 30m.
- Rollback: auto-roll back if (a) apac spare capacity recovers to >10% OR (b) cost burn > 12% above baseline for 45m.

Action items (owner / due)
- Diego: implement hedging toggle and automation script + smoke test (due 2026-08-24).
- Priya: instrument template-level tracing and dashboard; add prewarm ROI widget (due 2026-08-22).
- Liam: open PR for autobalancer bias + runbench (PR #278 link in artifacts) (due 2026-08-20).
- Maya: cost simulation and finance note; confirm budget for hedging window (due 2026-08-21).
- Aria: coordinate legal check for cross-region reroute opt-outs; compile list of routes requiring opt-out (due 2026-08-21).

Notes / scratch ideas (informal)
- Could we do predictive hedging? feed upcoming calendar + marketing events into a light-weight demand predictor to auto-schedule hedges earlier in the day. Low priority but high ROI for product launches.
- Consider warm pool tiers: templated-high-frequency, templated-low-frequency, ad-hoc. Different prewarm thresholds per tier.
- Backfill policy: prefer GPU families with lower spot-eviction risk for backfill to reduce thrash.

Meeting adjourned. Next check-in: quick sync Wed 2026-08-20 11:00 PT to kick off hedging window and validate smoke tests.
